design_detail: Mendelian randomization, two-sample, using published summary statistics: up to 94 variants associated at genome-wide significance with alcohol consumption (log-transformed drinks per week) in a genome-wide study of 941 280 people of European descent (GSCAN; Liu et al., 2019, ref 16) as instruments, and variant-outcome associations from case-control genome-wide consortia (MEGASTROKE, CARDIoGRAMplusC4D, AFGen, ISGC) and from case/non-case analyses in UK Biobank, for eight primary cardiovascular diseases and three stroke types. Methods: random-effects inverse-variance weighted analysis (primary), weighted median, MR-PRESSO, MR-Egger, and multivariable Mendelian randomization adjusted for genetic liability to smoking initiation; the ADH1B rs1229984 variant alone as a secondary instrument; UK Biobank never-smokers as a sensitivity analysis. The methods are described in detail only in the Data Supplement (not read). Labelled case-control under the round brief's rule (outcome associations come from case-control genome-wide studies, with UK Biobank case/non-case data alongside) and appraised with ROBINS-E, because the protocol names no instrument for this design.
can_establish: Whether people genetically predisposed to drink more, in European-ancestry data, have higher odds of stroke, peripheral artery disease and six other cardiovascular diseases, by an approach less exposed than conventional studies to confounding by lifestyle and to reverse causation.
cannot_establish: The shape of the relationship, including any J- or U-shape (the authors say they could not examine it); the effect of a given number of drinks (estimates are per SD of log-transformed drinks per week, an SD not reported in the main text); effects in non-European populations; and whether part of the association runs through smoking (the instrument predicts smoking initiation) or through education (the ADH1B variant is associated with it).

sample.recruitment: Consortium and biobank data: published genome-wide summary statistics (GSCAN for alcohol consumption and smoking initiation; SSGAC for education; MEGASTROKE, CARDIoGRAMplusC4D, AFGen and ISGC for outcomes) and UK Biobank analyses under application 29202 (Figure 1; Acknowledgments).
sample.inclusion_exclusion: Variants associated with alcohol consumption at genome-wide significance in the exposure study; selection details are in the Data Supplement (not read).
sample.demographics: Exposure data from people of European descent; outcome consortia mostly of European ancestry, with stroke (MEGASTROKE) and atrial fibrillation (AFGen) results similar when restricted to European-descent participants (Table XII, not read). The alcohol-lowering rs1229984 allele has a frequency of 0.026 in UK Biobank (Discussion › Comparison With Other Studies, 1st paragraph).
sample.selection_effects: UK Biobank contributes to the exposure genome-wide study and to most outcome datasets, so samples overlap (the authors note possible bias). Case definitions and case selection differ between consortia; several outcomes have few cases (aortic valve stenosis 2244, abdominal aortic aneurysm 1094, subarachnoid haemorrhage 1084), and the ISGC intracerebral haemorrhage dataset is small (1545 cases, 1481 non-cases).

exposure.measurement: Genetic instrument for self-reported alcohol consumption in drinks per week, log-transformed, from the exposure genome-wide study (how drinks were defined and whether non-drinkers were included are in that study and the Data Supplement, not read). No individual-level intake was analysed.
exposure.dose_frequency_duration_route: All estimates are per 1-SD increase in log-transformed drinks per week; the size of that SD, and the grams it corresponds to, are not given in the main text. Instrument strength (F statistics) is not reported in the main text.
exposure.polysubstance: Genetically predicted drinking was associated with smoking initiation (OR 1.24, 1.15 to 1.33; P=9.5×10−9); multivariable Mendelian randomization adjusted for genetic liability to smoking initiation, and UK Biobank never-smokers were analysed separately (Table XI, not read). The ADH1B variant showed no association with smoking initiation (OR 0.97, 0.89 to 1.07; P=0.57).

comparison.controls: Non-cases in each outcome dataset (consortium controls, or UK Biobank participants without the condition); the genetic estimates compare people along a continuous scale of genetic predisposition to drink, with no drinking reference group.
comparison.unmeasured_premorbid: Education: weak association of the overall instrument with fewer years of schooling (β −0.09 years, −0.17 to 0.00; P=0.05) and a clearer one for the ADH1B variant (β −0.15, −0.23 to −0.08; P=5.4×10−5), which the authors note could create horizontal pleiotropy for coronary artery disease.

outcomes.instruments: Eight primary outcomes (stroke, coronary artery disease, atrial fibrillation, heart failure, venous thromboembolism, peripheral artery disease, aortic valve stenosis, abdominal aortic aneurysm); secondary: ischaemic stroke (with its subtypes in MEGASTROKE), intracerebral and subarachnoid haemorrhage; possible mediators (systolic and diastolic blood pressure, HDL and LDL cholesterol, triglycerides) and confounders (smoking initiation, education).
outcomes.validity_norms: Case definitions follow each consortium or UK Biobank coding (Data Supplement, not read).
outcomes.operationalization: Odds ratio of disease per 1-SD increase in log-transformed drinks per week (random-effects inverse-variance weighted); beta per SD for mediators.
outcomes.multiplicity_correction: None stated in the main text. 18 counts the eight primary and three secondary cardiovascular outcomes, five mediators and two confounders (plus four ischaemic stroke subtypes); associations with P near 0.05 are described as some or suggestive evidence.

analysis.effect_sizes: [Genetic; overall instrument; OR per 1-SD increase in log drinks/week; inverse-variance weighted / multivariable adjusted for smoking initiation] stroke 1.27 (95% CI 1.12 to 1.45; P=2.87×10−4) / 1.21 (1.05 to 1.40; P=0.010); coronary artery disease 1.16 (1.00 to 1.36; P=0.052) / 1.08 (0.91 to 1.27); atrial fibrillation 1.17 (1.00 to 1.37; P=0.050) / 1.11 (0.93 to 1.32); heart failure 1.00 (0.68 to 1.47) / 0.88 (0.57 to 1.37); venous thromboembolism 1.04 (0.77 to 1.39) / 1.05 (0.75 to 1.47); peripheral artery disease 3.05 (1.92 to 4.85; P=2.30×10−6) / 2.55 (1.49 to 4.35; P=6.09×10−4); aortic valve stenosis 1.03 (0.56 to 1.90) / 0.94 (0.46 to 1.91); abdominal aortic aneurysm 2.60 (1.15 to 5.89; P=0.022) / 2.29 (0.89 to 5.93; P=0.087) (Figure 3). Ischaemic stroke 1.26 (1.09 to 1.46; P=0.002) and intracerebral haemorrhage 3.53 (1.70 to 7.32; P=0.001), combining consortium and UK Biobank data (Figure 4). Mediators: systolic blood pressure 0.12 (0.05 to 0.20), diastolic 0.15 (0.05 to 0.25), HDL cholesterol 0.39 (0.25 to 0.53), LDL cholesterol −0.01 (−0.18 to 0.16), triglycerides −0.37 (−0.67 to −0.07) (Figure 2; the units printed there are doubtful, see reporting issues). [ADH1B rs1229984 only] ischaemic stroke 1.31 (1.05 to 1.65; P=0.018), intracerebral haemorrhage 11.5 (1.31 to 101.46; P=0.027).
analysis.covariates: Multivariable Mendelian randomization adjusted for genetic liability to smoking initiation.
analysis.preregistration_detail: No registration or analysis plan is reported.
analysis.selective_reporting: All eight primary outcomes are reported with both main methods (Figure 3); secondary methods, single-variant results and sensitivity analyses are in supplementary tables (not read).
analysis.power: Not reported; the authors note low precision for outcomes with few cases.

interpretation_gap.results_show: Genetic predisposition to drink more was associated with higher odds of stroke (1.27 per SD of log drinks/week), especially intracerebral haemorrhage (3.53), and of peripheral artery disease (3.05), and these associations remained after adjustment for genetic liability to smoking; associations with coronary artery disease, atrial fibrillation and abdominal aortic aneurysm were weaker and lost significance after smoking adjustment; there was no association with heart failure, venous thromboembolism or aortic valve stenosis.
interpretation_gap.claimed: The Conclusions report "evidence of a causal relationship" for stroke and peripheral artery disease. That wording depends on the Mendelian randomization assumptions holding; the authors' own data show that the instrument predicts smoking initiation, and the smoking-adjusted estimates are smaller. The peripheral artery disease result rests on 3415 UK Biobank cases, in a biobank that also contributed to the exposure study. The Discussion's remark that, because heavy drinking was uncommon in UK Biobank, the burden of risk is unlikely to be confined to heavy drinkers is an inference the linear analysis cannot test, since the authors concede they could not examine J- or U-shapes. The Discussion also says the overall instrument showed no association with education, where the Results report weak evidence (P=0.05). Otherwise the paper is cautious about coronary artery disease and the other outcomes.

timeline.event: Holmes et al. (European ancestry, ADH1B rs1229984): lower coronary heart disease odds in carriers of the intake-lowering allele; this paper says its own rs1229984 results for stroke and coronary artery disease largely confirm that study.

Millwood et al. (China Kadoorie Biobank, ALDH2 and ADH1B): positive genetic associations with stroke, stronger for intracerebral haemorrhage, and none with myocardial infarction; this paper says it extends the stroke findings to European ancestry.

Mukamal, Stampfer and Rimm, critique of Mendelian randomization evidence on alcohol and cardiovascular disease (listed in the project's DOI list); published before this paper and not read for this card.

Biddinger et al. (UK Biobank, scores for alcohol use disorder): linear Mendelian randomization associations with stroke (OR 1.26, 1.04 to 1.54) and coronary artery disease (1.38), citing this paper; both studies use UK Biobank outcome data, so the agreement is not independent replication.

replication.where_it_stands: For stroke, genetic studies in European and east Asian populations agree that higher genetically predicted intake goes with more stroke, more strongly with intracerebral haemorrhage (Millwood et al., 2019; this study). Peripheral artery disease and aortic aneurysm rest on single datasets with few cases and need replication outside UK Biobank. For coronary disease the genetic evidence is inconsistent across instruments and populations.

funding.affiliations_note: Uppsala University and Karolinska Institutet (S C Larsson, K Michaëlsson); Department of Public Health and Primary Care, MRC Biostatistics Unit and British Heart Foundation Cardiovascular Epidemiology Unit, University of Cambridge (S Burgess, A M Mason). what_would_settle_it: Replication of the peripheral artery disease, aortic aneurysm and intracerebral haemorrhage associations in outcome data independent of UK Biobank and of the exposure study, with instruments not associated with smoking; and nonlinear analyses of individual-level data to see whether the stroke association extends down to light intake.

domains.note: Instrument independence: European-descent exposure data and partly multi-ancestry outcome consortia (restricted analyses similar); the authors say population stratification cannot be ruled out. Exclusion restriction: the instrument predicts smoking initiation (OR 1.24) and the ADH1B variant predicts education; MR-Egger indicated directional pleiotropy only for aortic valve stenosis; weighted median, MR-PRESSO and multivariable analyses were used; the stroke and peripheral artery disease associations persisted after smoking adjustment and in never-smokers.

Relevance: variants at genome-wide significance in 941 280 people, but no F statistic in the main text; overlap of UK Biobank between exposure and outcome data can bias estimates towards the conventional association if instruments are weak (the authors note possible bias). Shape at low intake: the exposure scale (per SD of log drinks per week) cannot be converted into grams and the linear analysis cannot show what happens at low intake.

Selection into the source studies: case-control consortia and UK Biobank volunteers, with overlapping samples; recruitment into these studies is outside the authors' control and could relate to both drinking and disease.
Not applicable: the instrument is fixed at conception.
Not applicable to summary data beyond the use of outcomes with available genome-wide results.
Definitions vary between consortia and UK Biobank (Data Supplement, not read); misclassification is unlikely to depend on genotype and would mainly dilute associations.
Methods only in a supplement; no registered plan; 18 outcomes without a stated correction; all primary outcomes are nonetheless reported.

risk_of_bias.reasoning: A standard summary-data Mendelian randomization with a strong multi-variant instrument and the usual sensitivity analyses. For stroke and intracerebral haemorrhage the results are consistent across methods, after adjustment for smoking liability and with the ADH1B variant alone, and agree with the east Asian genetic data; for peripheral artery disease and aortic aneurysm they rest on few UK Biobank cases with sample overlap; for coronary artery disease and atrial fibrillation they are borderline and sensitive to smoking adjustment. Design label and instrument follow the round brief's rule for Mendelian randomization (the protocol is silent). Cite this card for: genetic evidence in European-ancestry data that higher genetically predicted alcohol intake is associated with higher odds of stroke (particularly intracerebral haemorrhage) and of peripheral artery disease. Do not cite it for: risk at a particular intake, the shape of the relation, or a firm effect on coronary artery disease, atrial fibrillation, heart failure, venous thromboembolism or aortic valve stenosis.

key_findings.finding: Data sources: instrument variants from a genome-wide study of alcohol consumption in 941 280 people of European descent; outcomes (cases/non-cases) stroke 76 814/812 384 (MEGASTROKE, UK Biobank), coronary artery disease 90 079/461 812 (CARDIoGRAMplusC4D, UK Biobank), atrial fibrillation 65 446/522 744 (AFGen), and from UK Biobank heart failure 6712/360 874, venous thromboembolism 14 097/353 489, peripheral artery disease 3415/364 171, aortic valve stenosis 2244/365 342 and abdominal aortic aneurysm 1094/366 492; ischaemic stroke 64 943/817 434, intracerebral haemorrhage 2609/368 003 (ISGC, UK Biobank), subarachnoid haemorrhage 1084/366 502; blood pressure up to 367 284 and lipids up to 350 162 individuals (UK Biobank); smoking initiation 632 802 (GSCAN); education 766 345 (SSGAC).
key_findings.note: Values printed in the Figure 1 diagram (an image), read from the full-size figure image.

key_findings.finding: Possible mediators (overall instrument; beta per SD increase of log drinks per week; random-effects inverse-variance weighted): systolic blood pressure 0.12 (0.05 to 0.20; P=0.001; 346 656 people), diastolic 0.15 (0.05 to 0.25; P=0.003; 367 284), HDL cholesterol 0.39 (0.25 to 0.53; P=6.10×10−8; 320 717), LDL cholesterol −0.01 (−0.18 to 0.16; P=0.900; 349 795), triglycerides −0.37 (−0.67 to −0.07; P=0.016; 350 162).
key_findings.locator: Results › Associations With Potential Mediators and Confounders, 1st paragraph; Figure 2
key_findings.note: Values printed beside the forest plot in Figure 2 (an image), read from the full-size image; the units labelled there (mm Hg, mmol/L) are doubtful (see reporting issues).

key_findings.finding: Possible confounders: the overall instrument was strongly associated with smoking initiation (OR 1.24, 1.15 to 1.33; P=9.5×10−9) and weakly with education (β −0.09 years of schooling, −0.17 to 0.00; P=0.05). The ADH1B rs1229984 instrument was associated with higher systolic and diastolic blood pressure and LDL cholesterol, not with HDL cholesterol or triglycerides, not with smoking initiation (OR 0.97, 0.89 to 1.07; P=0.57), and with less education (β −0.15, −0.23 to −0.08; P=5.4×10−5).
key_findings.locator: Results › Associations With Potential Mediators and Confounders, 1st and 2nd paragraphs

key_findings.finding: Cardiovascular diseases (overall instrument; OR per SD increase of log drinks per week; inverse-variance weighted, then adjusted for genetic liability to smoking initiation): stroke 1.27 (1.12 to 1.45; P=2.87×10−4), adjusted 1.21 (1.05 to 1.40; P=0.010); peripheral artery disease 3.05 (1.92 to 4.85; P=2.30×10−6), adjusted 2.55 (1.49 to 4.35; P=6.09×10−4); coronary artery disease 1.16 (1.00 to 1.36; P=0.052), adjusted 1.08 (0.91 to 1.27; P=0.389); atrial fibrillation 1.17 (1.00 to 1.37; P=0.050), adjusted 1.11 (0.93 to 1.32; P=0.237); abdominal aortic aneurysm 2.60 (1.15 to 5.89; P=0.022), adjusted 2.29 (0.89 to 5.93; P=0.087); heart failure 1.00 (0.68 to 1.47; P=0.996), adjusted 0.88 (0.57 to 1.37); venous thromboembolism 1.04 (0.77 to 1.39; P=0.810), adjusted 1.05 (0.75 to 1.47); aortic valve stenosis 1.03 (0.56 to 1.90; P=0.926), adjusted 0.94 (0.46 to 1.91).
key_findings.locator: Results › Associations With CVD, 1st paragraph; Figure 3; Abstract
key_findings.note: The smoking-adjusted estimates are printed only in Figure 3 (an image), read from the full-size image; the text says only that they were somewhat attenuated.

key_findings.finding: Sensitivity analyses: directional pleiotropy (MR-Egger) was indicated only for aortic valve stenosis; weighted median and MR-Egger analyses suggested positive associations with aortic valve stenosis; stroke and coronary artery disease estimates were similar using consortium data only and UK Biobank data only; in UK Biobank never-smokers the estimates resembled the smoking-adjusted ones, except that the coronary artery disease estimate was larger (OR 1.39, 0.98 to 1.96; P=0.064).

Stroke types (overall instrument, per SD of log drinks per week): ischaemic stroke 1.26 (1.09 to 1.46; P=0.002) combining MEGASTROKE and UK Biobank; intracerebral haemorrhage 3.53 (1.70 to 7.32; P=0.001) combining ISGC and UK Biobank. By source: MEGASTROKE any ischaemic stroke 1.26 (1.08 to 1.48), large artery 1.30 (0.93 to 1.82), small vessel 1.20 (0.88 to 1.64), cardioembolic 1.11 (0.79 to 1.56); UK Biobank ischaemic stroke 1.24 (0.84 to 1.84), subarachnoid haemorrhage 2.47 (1.08 to 5.62), intracerebral haemorrhage 3.81 (1.57 to 9.27); ISGC intracerebral haemorrhage 3.00 (0.83 to 10.82; 1545 cases, 1481 non-cases).
key_findings.locator: Results › Associations With CVD, 2nd paragraph; Figure 4
key_findings.note: Source-specific estimates are printed in Figure 4 (an image), read from the full-size image.

key_findings.finding: With rs1229984 in ADH1B as the only instrument, genetically predicted drinking was associated (all P<0.05) with higher odds of any stroke, coronary artery disease, peripheral artery disease, aortic valve stenosis and abdominal aortic aneurysm; ischaemic stroke OR 1.31 (1.05 to 1.65; P=0.018), intracerebral haemorrhage 11.5 (1.31 to 101.46; P=0.027). Excluding rs1229984 from the overall instrument gave results similar to the full set.

Limitations stated by the authors: low precision for outcomes with few cases; UK Biobank in the variant-discovery, exposure and outcome datasets, which may bias estimates (stroke and coronary results were similar with consortium data only, and with rs1229984, which was not discovered in UK Biobank); population stratification not excluded; and no possibility of examining U- or J-shaped associations, so no statements about moderate versus heavy drinking.

reporting_issues.issue: Venous thromboembolism non-cases are given as 353 489 in Figure 1 and as 353 589 in Figure 3.
reporting_issues.consequence: Minor inconsistency; quote the case count (14 097), which agrees.

reporting_issues.issue: The Results report weak evidence of an association of the overall instrument with education (β −0.09, −0.17 to 0.00; P=0.05), while the Discussion says no association of the overall instrument with education was found.
reporting_issues.page: PMC HTML, Results › Associations With Potential Mediators and Confounders, 1st paragraph; Discussion › Strengths and Limitations, 1st paragraph
reporting_issues.consequence: The education check is borderline rather than clean; pleiotropy through education is not excluded for the overall instrument.

reporting_issues.issue: Figure 2 labels blood pressure in mm Hg and HDL cholesterol in mmol/L, but the estimates (0.12 mm Hg systolic, 0.39 mmol/L HDL per SD of log drinks per week) are implausible together in those units, suggesting standardized units; the units are not explained in the main text (Table VIII of the supplement not read).
reporting_issues.consequence: The mediator estimates cannot be quoted with units until the supplement is checked; only their direction is safe to cite.

reporting_issues.issue: The exposure is scaled per 1-SD increase in log-transformed drinks per week throughout, but the size of that SD is not given in the main text.
reporting_issues.consequence: The odds ratios cannot be translated into drinks or grams; claims must keep the per-SD wording.

reporting_issues.issue: The Discussion describes its coronary dataset as having about three times as many cases as Holmes et al. (20 259), while Figure 1 lists 90 079 coronary artery disease cases, about 4.4 times as many (editors' arithmetic); the dataset used for the rs1229984 analysis is not specified in the main text (Table XIII, not read).
reporting_issues.page: PMC HTML, Discussion › Comparison With Other Studies, 1st paragraph; Figure 1
reporting_issues.consequence: Minor; the rs1229984 coronary result may come from a subset of the outcome data.
